map.Lessons 7-1 & 7-2 — part of the Below Ze: Lessons 7-1 & 7-2. Part of the Below Zero arc. integers & opposites · ordering rationals · 6.NOS.C.5–7. Read it all the way. Each gate gives hints and a worked example. It does not stop you.
map.Episode 1. Same crew, same city — one fo: Episode 1. Same crew. Same city. One part of the case. Turn the page when you are set.
map.The whole grid went dark at 6:14. Jamal: The whole grid went dark at 6:14. Jamal, you and I lead. Get the notebook and the clues.
map.Fact one: Ada Vex built the Pattern Engi: Fact one: Ada Vex built the Pattern Engine. It is at Meridian Avenue and Zero Street. The heart of town.
map.Her street grid IS a coordinate plane. T: Her street grid IS a coordinate plane. The engine is at the origin, (0, 0). Power goes out from zero. One part of town at a time.
map.East–west streets count along the x-axis: East–west streets use the x-axis. North–south streets use the y-axis. Where they cross is the origin.
map.Vexhall Observatory steps. The old brass: Vexhall Observatory steps. The old brass gauge still works. Just.
map.Down to −8° tonight. Yesterday's high wa: It drops to −8° tonight. Yesterday's high was 5°. The cellar stays at −3°.
map.Below-zero numbers. Whole ones with no f: Numbers less than zero. All whole. No fraction. Integers, right?
map.Correct. Integers: counting numbers, the: Yes. Integers are counting numbers, their opposites, and zero. Opposites are the same distance from zero. They sit on the other side. The heat router dial must show the opposite of −7. Then it wakes.
map.An integer is a whole number, its opposi: An integer: a whole number, its opposite, or zero. −8, −3, 0, and 5 are all integers.
map.Reader — you're our fifth crew member. L: Reader, you are on our crew too! Log the numbers. Spin the dial!
map.The heat router needs yesterday's log. P: The heat router needs yesterday's log. Pick a chip. Then tap its tick mark: −8°, −3°, and 5°. Then wake the router. Its dial must show the opposite of −7. Type that number.
map.Conceptual: zero is the freezing mark. N: Conceptual: zero is the freeze mark. Negative numbers go BELOW zero. The more negative, the LOWER the tick. Opposites are the same distance from zero. They sit on the other side.
map.Procedural: start at 0 and count ticks D: Procedural: start at 0. For a negative number, count ticks DOWN. −3 is three ticks below zero. For an opposite, keep the distance from zero. Switch the side.
map.Heater trucks roll to the coldest distri: Heat trucks go to the coldest place first. But which one IS coldest? One number is a fraction.
map.Don't trust your eyes. Under a minus sig: Do not trust your eyes. With a minus sign, big digits mean very cold.
map.All four are rational numbers — any numb: All four are rational numbers. You can write each as a fraction. Like −2.5 or −¾. They look different. They share one number line.
map.Rational numbers include integers, fract: Rational numbers can be integers, fractions, or decimals. Positive or negative. Least is the one most far below zero.
map.Sort the ledger, reader — the coldest di: Put the list in order, reader. The coldest place gets the first truck!
map.Four district readings: −2.5°, 0.5°, −3°: Four numbers from four parts of town: −2.5°, 0.5°, −3°, −¾°. Tap them in order from least to greatest. Coldest goes first. Tap a card again to undo it.
map.Conceptual: colder means farther BELOW z: Conceptual: colder means farther BELOW zero. On a number line, the least is far left. A minus sign with a big digit is cold.
map.Procedural: rewrite everything the same: Procedural: first, write each number the same way. As a decimal, three fourths is 0.75, so −¾ = −0.75. Then go along the number line, left to right.
map.The full story — Below Zero — is glowing: The full story is Below Zero. It waits at the gate. — A.V.

map.Place −6° on a thermometer: start at the: Put −6° on the scale. Start at the 0 mark. Count six ticks down. That tick is −6.
map.Its opposite keeps the same distance — s: Its opposite is the same distance, six. But it is on the other side. Six ticks UP lands on 6.
map.So −6 and 6 are opposites: same distance: So −6 and 6 are opposites. Same distance from zero. Opposite ways.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
Write them as decimals: −1.5, 1, −0.5, −2. The one farthest below zero is −2. That is the least.
map.Left to right: −2, −1.5, −0.5, 1. Negati: Left to right: −2, −1.5, −0.5, 1. Negatives can trick you. Check how far below zero each one is.
map.Place all three readings on the thermome: First, put all three numbers on the scale. Tap a chip, then a tick.
map.A negative reading lives BELOW the zero: A negative number goes BELOW the zero mark. Check which side of 0 your tick is on.
map.−8 is COLDER than −3 — deeper below zero: −8 is COLDER than −3. It is farther down. So its tick is LOWER.
map.At least one reading sits on the wrong t: One or more numbers are on the wrong tick. Count the ticks from 0 with care.
map.Readings logged, dial at 7 — the heat ro: Numbers logged. The dial is at 7. The heat router hums awake!
map.Readings placed! Now the dial: an opposi: Numbers placed! Now the dial. An opposite keeps the distance from zero. It flips the side.
Tap all four. Coldest goes first.
−3 < −2.5 < −¾ < 0.5 — Frostvale first. The heat trucks go out. Coldest part of town first!
map.Careful — −¾ is only ¾ below zero. −2.5: Look again. −¾ is just ¾ below zero. −2.5 is two and a half below. Colder is lower.
map.Not coldest-to-warmest yet. Picture all: Not coldest to warmest yet. See all four on a number line. Then tap.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
